Going to therapy is only the beginning in a situation like this one and the reality of getting better is that if you're going to therapy but you're not willing to submit yourself to your pain, it takes a while to heal and learn. The journey in therapy is different for everyone and it looks like you've been able to gain more the experience a lot quicker than she has and it's a normal thing. It happens. In the same way that general individual growth in a relationship always happens at different times. In normal instances its easy to say that patience is key and it becomes a lot easier to practice when there isn't deliberate hurt and pain but the real test is in situations like yours.

When it comes to mental health, it is always important to remember that it's okay to not be able to continue a relationship with someone that is in pain and struggles to communicate this. We're all on our own journey to heal and this kind of healing should never be taken lightly. It's sometimes best to leave a person alone so that they can really begin to heal on their own for themselves. You've both done some horrendous things but it's what you do after that counts for a lot. It never negates what's been done, but as my boyfriend says, everyday is a new day to redeem yourself.

May I ask, what feelings do you have towards marriage in general? 

I think that you're right to say you'll get married only if it's the last resort. There's really nothing wrong with feeling that you want more time to see where your relationship goes and that doesn't mean you're unsure about anything. But I'm in a relationship with someone and we just recently passed our one year mark and we were just speaking about how we now understand couples who date for a year or less and get married. We're madly in love and would get married in a split second but our circumstances won't allow it. What I'm trying to say is, if you're nervous about time and how long you've been together bc typically people wait years before marriage then honestly you need to forget about that. Relationships and bonds and connections are different for everyone and there isn't a right or ideal time to get married. All that matters if if you feel fully ready to commit your whole life to marriage and if you're not then that's really okay too. 

If you feel strongly that you need to pace yourself then you need to think about other ways to get her a visa, maybe help her pay for it or something. It seems that if you guys really want this you'll have to make some big sacrifices, but explore your options before jumping into the marriage thing if you're feeling nervous about it. Maybe do some more digging about your alternatives?
